findings.title: Drain recovery-time input after native registration completes
findings.impact: Input accumulated while the recovered attachment is still registering can become a fresh ownership request on the new controller. For example, withhold the recovery controller-create response, queue Prefix/Ctrl-L, then release the response: the resumed event loop processes those keys and can acquire an unowned target or create a reservation against its existing owner without a fresh post-recovery gesture. This breaks the promised discard of queued recovery input even though recovered() disables polling-based auto-acquisition.
findings.evidence: The only recovered-event drain is at tui.rs:977–998. It runs before display/resize setup and NativeControl::register at line 1008. register performs snapshot and controller-create RPCs at tui/control.rs:164–173, leaving a blocking input-accumulation interval after that drain. No later setup drain exists, and tick is initialized anew at tui.rs:1049. The queued Prefix/Ctrl-L is consumed by tui.rs:1403–1413, calling NativeControl::open; its observer branch calls request at control.rs:940, which enqueues Work::Claim at lines 950–966. The worker has a fresh heartbeat, so the pause guard does not reject this setup-time input.
findings.fix: Perform the bounded recovered-input drain after native registration and the remaining blocking setup, before recovered events can reach authority/application routing. Preserve safe quit and fail-closed overflow behavior. Add a controlling-PTY regression that holds the recovery registration response, queues Prefix/Ctrl-L during that interval, then verifies unchanged owner/reservation and no ownership-claim emission after registration completes.
